title: Saying things with print()
objective: Use print() to show text on the screen.
explanation_md:
## The print() function

`print()` is a built-in tool in Python that **shows things on the screen** (in your console).

The word inside the brackets is what you want to show.

```python
print("Hello, world!")
```

A few rules:

- The text must go inside **quotes** — either `"double"` or `'single'`.
- The brackets `(` and `)` must be there.
- You can use `print()` as many times as you like; each one goes on its own line.

## Your turn

Make Python print this **exact** message:

> `I am learning Python`

No extra words, no quotes around it in the output.
exercise_prompt: Print exactly: I am learning Python
hints: Put the text in quotes: print("...")
The text inside the quotes should be: I am learning Python
